correctness.rationale: The restricted gradient forces equal squares; the hyperplane condition in characteristic five forces all five signs equal. The local quadratic form has matrix I+J of determinant 4. In the displayed coordinates the equation is TQ=H, and the three factors of H cut Q transversely in six distinct F_5-points. The inverse projection is the blowup of the base ideal (Q,H); in its Q-chart the map is the graph H/Q away from the contracted strict transform of Q, a (−2)-curve. The six exceptional divisors are node-lines. For a line avoiding the node, adjunction and anticanonical degree give the displayed degree and multiplicity conditions; Cauchy–Schwarz gives plane degree at most two. Two-point chords supply the fifteen lines, and Bézout rules out a conic through just five of the six points. The two permutation orbits cover all lines. Full Jacobian rank gives local length one away from the node. For the node-line, three equations eliminate three variables formally and the remaining equation has zero linear part and nonzero quadratic term 3t² on the kernel, so higher-order corrections to eliminated variables cannot cancel that term. This gives the dual numbers over F_5. Properness and finite fibers imply finiteness over the DVR, and equal generic and special lengths imply flatness. Over a strict henselization the summand at each special point has rank its special length and reduced geometric generic fiber, giving the claimed pairwise mergers. The blowup and contraction change the plane point count by 6q and −q respectively, yielding the formula for every q=5^m.
residual_risks: Rational enumeration does not rule out geometric lines unknown over F_5 or establish flatness or the all-extension zeta function; the written geometric and local proofs do. Frozen code was not executed.
